link.note: Identity as Catherine's mother confirmed by the 1850 census; maiden name 'Watson' only probable (Find a Grave index 'Julia A Watson Scott'); her parents speculative.

summary: John's 4th-great-grandmother; wife of Stephen Scott of Kingston, probably born Watson.
bio:
Julia Ann was 41 and born in Pennsylvania in the 1850 Kingston census (so born c.1809; tree 1809-1893 as a 'Potential' hint). Bradsby (1893) said she was born in Connecticut and was 94 and living in 1893 (implying c.1799), which Round 3 judged wrong on ages. FamilySearch (KG4S-GMT) gives her death in Oct 1893 and burial at Forty Fort Cemetery on 10 Oct 1893. The maiden name 'Watson' was unsourced in Rounds 1-2; Round 3 found the Find a Grave index on FamilySearch reading 'Julia A Watson Scott', Forty Fort (probable). FamilySearch makes her a daughter of George Watson (b. Mansfield, Notts., 6 Apr 1778; Huntington Twp 1810, Dallas 1820; d. 1830 Fairmount Springs) but pairs him with Ann Nancy Waterman (b. Norwich CT 1780, d. Barrington RI 1809), who had her own Julia Ann Watson b. Bristol RI 17 Jul 1809 - a clear merge of two families. No Scots-Irish evidence was found for either Scott or Watson.

Widowed in 1856, Julia Ann was living in Plymouth Township in July 1860, aged 50, working as a domestic, with her youngest daughter Ann ([R4-S1]). Her daughter Catherine told the 1910 census that both her parents were born in Connecticut ([R4-S2]), which agrees with Bradsby (1893) but not with the 1850 and 1860 censuses (Pennsylvania).

On her parentage, the FamilySearch tree's George Watson (b. Mansfield, Notts., 1778; Huntington Twp 1810, Dallas 1820, d. 1830) is mixed up with a Rhode Island family, as round 3 found ([R4-S3]). The tree's other children for George include Jairus Harrison Watson (b. Plymouth 1812, d. New Albany, Bradford Co., 1893), who married a Rebecca Van Loon, and Sabina (Watson) Partington, a widow living in Plymouth Twp in 1850-80 and born in Pennsylvania about 1802 ([R4-S3], [R4-S4]). A second candidate emerges from the county histories: Amariah (or Amaziah) Watson was a Plymouth taxable in 1796, alongside Michael Scott, Samuel Pringle and the Lamoreuxs ([R4-S5]); he had married the widow of Noah Buck, a Connecticut settler killed in the 1778 battle ([R4-S6]); and the Huntington Township history says that 'Amaziah Watson settled just below the Scott house, on the Huntington creek road' ([R4-S6]) - the 'old Scott house' built by Obadiah Scott on Huntington Creek ([R4-S6]). That puts a Watson family next to a Scott family in Huntington Twp, where the Pringles were later buried in the Scott Cemetery at Huntington Mills. Neither man is yet proven as Julia's father.

openQuestions: Prove maiden name Watson and parents: her Oct 1893 death notice in the Wilkes-Barre papers; Forty Fort cemetery records; Connecticut Barbour Collection for a Scott-Watson marriage c.1815-28.

Was Julia Ann a daughter of Amariah/Amaziah Watson (Plymouth 1796; Huntington Twp, next to the Scott house) rather than of George Watson? Check the 1800-1820 Plymouth/Huntington censuses for Amariah Watson's household and any Luzerne deed or Orphans' Court record naming his children.
1910 census says her birthplace was Connecticut - check Connecticut (Barbour) records for a Julia Ann Watson b. c.1809.

Round 4 searched without result: Full text of Bradsby 1893, Munsell 1880, Harvey Book, Pearce, Wright: no 'George Watson' of Huntington/Dallas mentioned; Luzerne wills index: no George or Amariah Watson will (Watson wills only from 1874 on)

Round 4: found her as a widow in Plymouth Twp in 1860 and identified Amariah Watson (Plymouth 1796; settled beside the Scott house in Huntington Twp) as an alternative candidate father to the FS George Watson.
